iPadOS 27.2 will release its beta version this week. In addition to introducing the redesigned Health app, Apple is also bringing over a recently launched feature from Mac: a Siri window that pops up when text is selected.

iPadOS 27.2 adds the feature of a Siri window popping up when text is selected, aligning with macOS Golden Gate

Siri AI is the headline feature of iOS 27, iPadOS 27 and related updates. As such, Apple offers multiple ways to use this upgraded assistant.

On the iPad, you can wake Siri with voice commands like 「喂 Siri」or 「Hey Siri」, pull it down from the top of the screen, use the new Siri option in the edit menu, open the brand-new Siri app, or my favourite method: press CMD + Space to bring up Spotlight, then ask Siri from there.

However, iPadOS 27.2 adds yet another option, brought over directly from the Mac.

In macOS 27 Golden Gate, in many situations, when you select a passage of text, a small Siri icon appears in the top-left corner of the selection. When you hover the cursor over the icon, it expands and shows an 「Ask Siri」text input field.

This feature was not available in iPadOS 27. But now, as long as you connect a trackpad to your iPad, iPadOS 27.2 delivers the same effect.

As shown in the image above, the new Siri icon is initially very small and won't get in your way, but as soon as you hover your cursor over it, the 「Ask Siri」input field pops up instantly, which is very convenient.

If no trackpad is connected, the full edit menu will still appear when text is selected, letting you tap to open Siri. That said, the experience is smoother and more seamless when used with a trackpad.

macOS has quite a few of these small but productivity-boosting features that can speed up daily operations, and iPadOS has long lacked these. Therefore, it's great to see this new Mac feature brought to the iPad.

What do you think of the new Siri pop-up window in iPadOS 27.2? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
